quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of other vehicles.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always stop completely before entering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging. Match the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Always yield to other vehicles when entering.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the gas. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull safely to the side of the road.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space to turn as cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and behind. Stay away from these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars do.

questions.question: Your gas pedal sticks open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Turn off the ignition by moving the switch just enough to stop the engine. Do not fully turn it or the steering wheel will lock. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors often.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder. Never rely on mirrors alone to see your blind spots.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and broken yellow line mark the road, with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
If traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass if no oncoming traffic is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds. This sign tells you a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop at a red or yellow light.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need depends on road conditions, weather, and how much traffic is coming toward you.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should you use?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are made for small children who cannot wear regular safety belts. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat to secure a child in a vehicle.

questions.question: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck sign and no gates or lights, you should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can hear an approaching train.
Only go when a flagger tells you it is safe, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and cannot see all lanes. You should:

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move forward into each lane as it becomes clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and safe to enter.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left, then right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely make these curves.

questions.question: The posted speed limit shows:

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit in bad weather or poor road conditions.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to ride home with someone who does not drink. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your body. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Which statement about passing is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror before returning to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, always signal at least 100 feet in advance. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your mirror.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:

options.text: Your parking lights.
Your low beam headlights.
Your high beam headlights.
Any lights available.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 and older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: A term for blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A term for blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
Just as dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see, headlights from other cars can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently by applying the brakes. When at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the steering wheel to force the vehicle back.

questions.question: What should drivers do when approaching a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Increase their speed.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on their headlights.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.
